explainedBy: The premortem as a deed: the listener writes down, in advance, the story of why the decision failed.

storyboard.claim: Assume total failure, then write the history of why it failed.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The listener, worried, holding the page he is writing the failure story on.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From defining the premortem to doing it.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the premortem is a written exercise.

explainedBy: Darwin married Emma and they loved each other: the two of them embrace.

storyboard.claim: Darwin married Emma Wedgwood; they had a deep, loving relationship.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Darwin and Emma embrace, both smiling.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the premortem to a human example: Darwin's marriage.
storyboard.addedInformation: Introduces Emma and the bond that is about to be tested.

explainedBy: Years later the couple loses their daughter: the two grieving adults beside a grave.

storyboard.claim: Years later they suffered a profound tragedy: the death of their daughter.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A grave; Darwin and Emma slumped and sad beside it.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The loving couple now grieves.
storyboard.addedInformation: The grave shows a death in the family without staging it.

explainedBy: The grave is their 10-year-old Annie's; Emma, in front now, grieves while Darwin stands behind her.

storyboard.claim: Their bright 10-year-old Annie died of illness; the loss fractured their lives.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The same grave; Emma now in front, sad, Darwin behind.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Names whose grave it is; Emma moves to the front.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: the name and age come from the callout.

explainedBy: Annie's death destroys Darwin's faith: Darwin at the grave, angry at a God who let his child suffer.

storyboard.claim: Annie's death destroyed what was left of Darwin's faith.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The same grave; Darwin in front with a bitter, angry face.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From shared grief to Darwin's own reaction.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: loss of faith is carried by the callout and the bitter face.

callout.text: He lost faith, she held on

explainedBy: The same loss splits the couple in opposite directions: Charles to non-belief, Emma to faith.

storyboard.claim: Darwin became a materialist non-believer; Emma went the opposite way.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A two-bucket sorter: Charles non-believer, Emma deeper faith.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From Darwin alone to the split between the two.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the two opposite responses side by side.

explainedBy: Emma survives her grief by holding on: she clutches her daughter's photo by the grave, trusting she will see her again.

storyboard.claim: To survive the grief Emma clung tighter to faith and the hope of seeing Annie again.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Emma, sad, holding a photo beside the grave.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Zooms into Emma's side of the split.
storyboard.addedInformation: The held photo shows she holds on to the lost daughter.

explainedBy: Emma's faith is the only thing keeping her afloat, and Darwin, beside her, now faces a decision that could take it away.

storyboard.claim: Faith was her only raft; in this fragile peace Darwin faced a career decision.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Emma still holding the photo; Darwin enters beside her, worried.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Darwin joins the kept stage: the decision is about to land on her.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: the raft metaphor is text only.

explainedBy: Darwin holds his drafted manuscript, a decision his old two-column list cannot settle.

storyboard.claim: No pro-con list could resolve it: he had the drafted manuscript of his theory of evolution.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Darwin, worried, holding the manuscript pages beside the pros-and-cons list.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From Emma's grief to Darwin's decision.
storyboard.addedInformation: Brings back his marriage list and the manuscript.

explainedBy: Darwin knows the manuscript he holds is the most important scientific idea of the millennium.

storyboard.claim: He knew it was the most important scientific idea of the millennium.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Darwin, proud, still holding the manuscript; a lightbulb for the big idea.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same manuscript; his face turns to pride in the idea.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the weight of the idea in his hands.

explainedBy: Publishing the manuscript would wound the faith his grieving wife lives on: Darwin holds it while Emma slumps beside him.

storyboard.claim: Publishing would strike a fatal blow to the doctrines his grieving wife relied on.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Darwin, worried, holding the manuscript; Emma beside him, sad and slumped.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Emma enters: the cost of the idea he holds.
storyboard.addedInformation: Puts the manuscript and the wife it would hurt in one frame.

explainedBy: Cause and effect: his professional triumph would shatter his wife's personal universe.

storyboard.claim: His professional triumph would shatter his wife's personal universe.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A flow: Publish his theory -> Wife's universe shattered.
storyboard.onScreenText: Publish his theory -> Wife's universe shattered
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the picture of the couple to the causal chain.
storyboard.addedInformation: States the trade-off as cause and effect.

explainedBy: Darwin's premortem extends the chain: publishing could end in a destroyed marriage.

storyboard.claim: A premortem on publishing meant facing the real possibility of destroying his marriage.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The same flow gains a third step: Marriage destroyed.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: One more step added to the kept flow.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the premortem's worst-case end point.

explainedBy: The feared outcome: Darwin reaches toward Emma, who has turned away traumatized, and he dies estranged from her.

storyboard.claim: Traumatizing Emma and dying alienated from the person he loved most.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Darwin sadly reaching toward Emma, who slumps away.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the chain to the couple living its end.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the estrangement as one reaching, one withdrawn.

explainedBy: The listener's own big commitment: he holds the 10-year lease he is about to sign.

storyboard.claim: Say you are about to sign a 10-year lease or a 50/50 partnership with your oldest friend.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The listener, uneasy, holding the lease document.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From Darwin to the listener's life.
storyboard.addedInformation: Makes the high-stakes commitment a document in hand.

explainedBy: The premortem jumps ahead in time: the listener, lease still in hand, looks three years forward.

storyboard.claim: A premortem makes you mentally time travel 3 years into the future.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Same listener with the lease; a clock appears for the jump in time.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Adds the clock: the time jump.
storyboard.addedInformation: The clock marks the move forward in time.

explainedBy: The imagined failure: the partnership ends in a lawsuit, the two partners angry at each other.

storyboard.claim: Imagine the partnership ended in a bitter lawsuit; now name the clashes and missing boundaries.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The listener and his partner angrily facing each other under a law icon.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The imagined future arrives: the failure itself.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the failed partnership as a legal fight between two people.

explainedBy: The premortem sorts the causes of the failure: personality clashes, missing boundaries, macroeconomic forces.

storyboard.claim: Identify the clashes, the lack of boundaries, or the macroeconomic forces that caused it.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A sorter of three causes of failure.
storyboard.onScreenText: Personality clashes / No boundaries / Market forces
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the failure to its listed causes.
storyboard.addedInformation: Lays out the premortem's output as parts.

explainedBy: The objection: asking a team to picture the startup crashing feels toxic, so the listener slumps at the picture of the crash.

storyboard.claim: Imagining our startup crashing on the eve of launch feels toxic and pessimistic.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The listener slumped and worried beside a crash icon.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the method to the objection to it.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the imagined crash and its deflating effect.

explainedBy: The objection continues: dwelling on the crash drains the belief and energy a venture needs.

storyboard.claim: It kills the momentum, belief and positive energy a venture needs.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Same crash icon; the listener's worry sinks to sadness.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same stage; the face drops from worried to sad.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: the loss of momentum is carried by the face and callout.

explainedBy: The reframe: the premortem looks pessimistic but sits at the optimism end of the scale.

storyboard.claim: It feels like a buzzkill, but the premortem is the ultimate form of strategic optimism.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A spectrum from pessimistic buzzkill to strategic optimism, marker near optimism.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the objection to the rebuttal.
storyboard.addedInformation: Places the premortem on the scale against first impressions.

explainedBy: Why it is optimistic: finding the failure points in advance leads to downstream flexibility.

storyboard.claim: Discovering failure points in advance gives you downstream flexibility.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A flow: Find failure points -> Downstream flexibility.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains the optimism as a mechanism.
storyboard.addedInformation: States the cause and its payoff.

explainedBy: Downstream flexibility means building shock absorbers into the plan, such as against a lease that could bankrupt you.

storyboard.claim: Downstream flexibility means building in shock absorbers, e.g. against a ruinous 10-year lease.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The same flow gains a third step: Shock absorbers.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: One more step added to the kept flow.
storyboard.addedInformation: Defines what the flexibility looks like.

explainedBy: The fail-safe in action: the listener now holds a shorter three-year lease with a break option instead of cancelling.

storyboard.claim: You don't cancel; you negotiate a three-year lease with an option to break it.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The listener, relieved, holding the new shorter lease.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Back to the lease from 279, now renegotiated.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: the shorter term is in the callout; the relieved face shows the fail-safe works.

explainedBy: Personal fail-safe: moving for love, the listener holds a rental key instead of buying a house.

storyboard.claim: Moving for a romance, rent a small apartment for a year instead of buying a house: an escape hatch.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The listener holding a key in front of a home.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From business lease to personal life.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: rent vs buy is carried by the callout; the key shows the new place.

explainedBy: The premortem does not stop you: the listener walks forward, protected if the move goes wrong.

storyboard.claim: The premortem doesn't paralyze you; it ensures you survive if the move goes wrong.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The listener walking forward with a shield beside him.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the fail-safe to its effect.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows moving forward while protected.

explainedBy: Widen the map: the listener, compass in hand, looks at the cliff edge instead of only the sunny path.

storyboard.claim: Don't map only the sunny path; widen the map to include the cliffs and the abyss.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The listener with a compass beside a cliff ledge.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Sums up the premortem as a wider map.
storyboard.addedInformation: The ledge shows the danger the map must include.

explainedBy: A recap of the steps so far: the variables are mapped and diverse voices broke the consensus trap.

storyboard.claim: We've mapped the variables and broken the consensus trap with diverse voices.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A sorter of the finished steps.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Recap of the divergence phase.
storyboard.addedInformation: Lists the steps covered so far.

explainedBy: The recap adds predicting multiple futures; then the divergence phase must end.

storyboard.claim: We've predicted multiple futures and done a premortem; the divergence phase has to end.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The same sorter gains a third bucket: Multiple futures.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: One more step added to the recap.
storyboard.addedInformation: Completes the list of divergence steps.

explainedBy: Now the decision has to be made: a tense living-room conversation between the author and his wife.

storyboard.claim: You have to make the choice; let's drop into a tense living-room conversation.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Johnson talking, worried; his wife slumped and worried in their living room.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the recap to the decision phase.
storyboard.addedInformation: Introduces the couple and the tension.

explainedBy: The choice is whether to uproot the family home: Johnson stands with a packed bag beside their home.

storyboard.claim: Johnson and his wife agonize over uprooting the family and moving from Brooklyn.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The same couple; a home icon and Johnson holding a packed briefcase.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same couple; the move enters as the home and the bag.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the question: leave home or stay.

explainedBy: Johnson's side of the stalemate: he points to the nature and weather of Marin while his wife looks unconvinced.

storyboard.claim: They are stuck; Steven focuses on the weather, hiking and natural beauty.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Johnson, happy, pointing at a tree; his wife worried.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Johnson states his side.
storyboard.addedInformation: The tree shows what pulls him to California.

explainedBy: Her side: the wife points to the walkable city of New York while Johnson looks doubtful.

storyboard.claim: His wife focuses on the pedestrian density of New York and its culture.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The wife, happy, pointing at a city; Johnson worried.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Mirror of 296: the other side, the other icon.
storyboard.addedInformation: City vs tree shows the two pulls.

explainedBy: What she would lose: she holds a photo of the friends they would leave behind.

storyboard.claim: Crucially, the tight-knit network of lifelong friendships they'd be leaving.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The wife, sad, holding a photo; Johnson worried.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same wife; her face turns sad and she holds the photo.
storyboard.addedInformation: The photo makes the friendships a thing she holds.

explainedBy: They are deadlocked weighing unlike things on one scale: both slumped beside the balance.

storyboard.claim: They are deadlocked weighing fundamentally asymmetrical things against each other.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A balance; Johnson and his wife both slumped and worried.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the two sides to the deadlock between them.
storyboard.addedInformation: The balance shows the weighing that cannot settle.

explainedBy: The impossible comparison: sunshine in one bucket, a best friend in the other.

storyboard.claim: How do you compare sunshine to a best friend? This is where linear value modeling comes in.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A sorter: Sunshine / A best friend.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Names the two things that cannot be weighed.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the asymmetry concretely.

explainedBy: Where the tool comes from: Jeremy Bentham's 19th-century philosophy of utilitarianism, shown as the book it came from.
noVisual: No figure for Bentham in the cast; the origin is carried by a book and the callout.

storyboard.claim: Linear value modeling is the mathematical offspring of Bentham's utilitarianism.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A book with the label Bentham's utilitarianism.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the problem to the tool's origin.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: the lineage is carried by the callout.

explainedBy: Johnson takes up a sheet to apply the method to their own choice, his wife beside him.

storyboard.claim: Greatest happiness for the greatest number; applied to a personal choice it works like this.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Johnson holding a sheet of notes, ready to work it out with his wife.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Back to the couple, now with a sheet to calculate on.
storyboard.addedInformation: Sets up the worked method on the next beats.
